# 14 Team Fantasy Basketball Mock Draft [9 Cat Mock Draft]

Locked On Fantasy Basketball, 2026-09-15, 52:07. https://youtu.be/KPdD91Oo8-U

## Summary

Josh Lloyd runs a live 14-team, 9-category mock draft with third round reversal, picking 12th. His main theme is that deeper leagues change strategy. Steady, low-upside players like Tobias Harris or Aaron Gordon become real starters, so you should hold off on flyers until about round 11. He also says players with big injury risk are dangerous picks around the eighth round because the replacement player is much worse in a deep league. His roster: Kevin Durant, Austin Reaves, Anthony Davis, Deni Avdija, Brandon Ingram, Coby White, Derik Queen, Cedric Coward, John Collins, Sandro Mamukelashvili, Yaxel Lendeborg, Aaron Nesmith, Nikola Vucevic and DeAndre Hunter. Basketball Monster projected his team fifth. Three of the top four picks projected in the top four even with third round reversal.

## Rules and methods

- [1:07](https://youtu.be/KPdD91Oo8-U?t=67) In deeper leagues, steady low-upside players like Aaron Gordon, Tobias Harris and Andrew Wiggins become key parts of your main roster instead of streaming spots.
  > "the guys that you would pass over Aaron Gordon Tobias Harris Andrew Wiggins maybe they become key parts"
- [1:22](https://youtu.be/KPdD91Oo8-U?t=82) In a 14-team league, do not start taking flyers too early, for example in round 8. Picks around 110 to 130 are active starters, not flyer picks.
  > "Do they start the flyers early and miss out on some solid picks? They start grabbing guys in round eight."
- [1:40](https://youtu.be/KPdD91Oo8-U?t=100) Players who are not worth rostering in 10 or 12 team leagues become your eighth or ninth best player in deeper leagues and gain value.
  > "They become your eighth best player, your ninth best player instead of being your 11th best player."
- [9:27](https://youtu.be/KPdD91Oo8-U?t=567) Standard score valuations depend on the mean and standard deviation of the player pool. As the pool grows from about 156 to 200, values shift and a player might move up around 10 spots.
  > "So it might not be big differences, but you might see someone push up 10 spots just due to player pool expanding."
- [12:19](https://youtu.be/KPdD91Oo8-U?t=739) The later you pick in a snake draft, the more risk you should accept, because the top of the draft has a built-in advantage.
  > "you got to increase your risk tolerance the further down the draft board you get because there is an inherent advantage"
- [12:25](https://youtu.be/KPdD91Oo8-U?t=745) Auction drafts are the best way to even out draft position. In snake formats, all-round reversal is the fairest: the first pick picks last in every other round.
  > "the best way to even it out obviously is an auction draft obviously."
- [14:20](https://youtu.be/KPdD91Oo8-U?t=860) Do not lock onto must-have players and reach for them. Make the best pick available and build around value.
  > "I can build a team around value, not hyperfocused targets."
- [19:26](https://youtu.be/KPdD91Oo8-U?t=1166) Do not draft a one-category specialist to fix a category that is already too weak to recover.
  > "his strength is steals. My steals are putrid. I wouldn't have recovered them from there."
- [27:53](https://youtu.be/KPdD91Oo8-U?t=1673) In a deep league, an injury-prone player taken around pick 110 is a big risk. When he misses games, a much worse replacement player has to start for you.
  > "when Porzingis misses, it means that my 11th best guy, which would be like the 170th, 180th best player, has to jump into my starting group."
- [28:51](https://youtu.be/KPdD91Oo8-U?t=1731) Picking first gives a safe core, so that manager can afford riskier picks later.
  > "you've got the security that you pick. So, you can take some risks. That's also the benefit of picking up at number one."
- [33:02](https://youtu.be/KPdD91Oo8-U?t=1982) Change your draft strategy based on how deep your league is.
  > "I think you should you should be changing your strategies in drafts depending on how deep your league actually is."
- [46:57](https://youtu.be/KPdD91Oo8-U?t=2817) Late in deep drafts, low-ceiling veterans are all upside at their price. Minutes upside drives value.
  > "I'm just give me minutes upside which is what Hunter has. Is he good? Of course not. But minutes will drive"
